data.name: Pharez
data.long_meaning: Derived from Hebrew bereshit, meaning 'in it is a mouth', or 'with a mouth it consumes'. In the Bible, Pharez is a son of Judah who was born from Tamar and was named after her pregnancy was revealed.

in_hebrew.name: פָּרֶץ
in_hebrew.long_meaning: פָּרֶץ (Parez) הוא שם נביא שנזכר במקרא, שמשמעותו 'תולדה, ערבוב, או פרץ'. פָּרֶץ הוא בן שמעון ועשה, בכורה של דוד. על-פי המסורת היה אחד משני בניו של דוד, האחר הוא נתן. כאשר רצח רצאל, שלא חפץ להכריז את שמעון כשבא, נתן, שהיה נתון בפחד, כי היה נשוי לעשה ולא חפץ להסתלק מבית אביו, היה נמלך לנהר ולפני שעלה, כי ראה, כי רצאל, יושב לו על-ראש הנחל, ושאל את-אלוהים, 'למה שכבר יצאת', ובתשובה נאמר לו, 'למען יהיה-שם' (1-סמואל, פּ, 1).

in_greek.name: Φαρές
in_greek.long_meaning: Φαρές (Phares) ὁ Ἡβραῖος, ἄνθρωπος σφόδρα εὐσεβής, οὗτος ἦν ὁ πρωτότοκος τοῦ Σαλμωνίου, καὶ οἱ Ἕλληνες αὐτόν ἔχουν Ὀμφαλόθεν, καὶ ἔτι ὁ Σαλμωνὴς ὁ Ἐβραῖος, τοῦ Ὀμφαλοῦ ὑπὸ τοῖς Ἕλλησιν, τὸν Φαρέσην οἰκτείρουν, καὶ τοὺς ἐκ τοῦ Φαρέσην οὐκ ἐξαίρετον, ἀλλ' ἐξουθενουμένους ἔχοντες, ὑπὸ τοῦ ἄλλου τοῦ Σαλμωνίου, τὸν Νὰθανῆν, οὐκ ἐξέλιπον, οὐδὲ ἀπώσαντο, ἀλλ' ἐκράτησαν, οὐ κατὰ τὴν ἀρχὴν, ἀλλὰ κατὰ τοῦ ἔθνους, τὸν Φαρέσην.

in_latin.long_meaning: Pharez, filius Salomonis, qui erat primogenitus ejus, et qui in libro Regum 1, 6, 17, nominatur, et qui in libro 1 Regum, cap. 3, 1, nominatur, et qui in libro 1 Regum, cap. 3, 4, nominatur, et qui in libro 1 Regum, cap. 3, 5, nominatur.

in_english.name: Pharez
in_english.meaning: firstborn son, son of Solomon, or a variant of Perez
in_english.long_meaning: Pharez is the name of a biblical figure, the son of Judah and the twin brother of Zerah. According to the biblical account, the twins were born while their mother, Tamar, was still pregnant with them. Before giving birth, Tamar gave birth to Pharez, but the midwife tied a scarlet thread to Zerah's hand, indicating that he was the firstborn. However, Pharez was actually the firstborn, and Zerah was the second-born. This story has been interpreted in various ways, but it is generally seen as a symbol of the struggle between good and evil, with Pharez representing good and Zerah representing evil. Pharez is also seen as a symbol of the Jewish people, who were considered to be the chosen people of God. The name Pharez has been used in various forms throughout history, including Pharez, Perez, and Pharès. In modern times, the name Pharez has been used as a given name, particularly in Christian families.

biblical_reference.note: Pharez is mentioned in the biblical account of the genealogy of Judah and the descendants of Jacob.

data.cultural_impact: The name Pharez is of Hebrew origin and has an interesting connection to the biblical story of one of Judah's sons. In this story, Pharez was born in a moment of shame and deception, yet went on to become an important figure in the lineage of King David and eventually, Jesus Christ. As such, the name Pharez carries a sense of overcoming adversity or challenging circumstances in one's own lineage or family.
data.spiritual_significance: Pharez's name is rooted in Hebrew, and its meaning emphasizes God's involvement in the events of human life. The name suggests that just as a mouth consumes food, God consumes our lives and sustains us. Additionally, the name can be seen as a reminder of God's power to bring good out of difficult circumstances and bless even those who may face shame and adversity in their lives.

historical_references.reference: Pharez was the name of one of the twin sons of Judah, the third son of Jacob, born to Tamar, Judah's daughter-in-law. This happened after Judah had slept with Tamar under the guise of disguising himself as a friend and giving her his signet, cord, and staff. Tamar later tricked Judah into sleeping with her again while he believed she was a prostitute, and she became pregnant with Pharez and his twin brother Zerah.
Pharez is also mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus Christ in the New Testament as an ancestor of Jesus through King David.

In the context of Judaic heritage and Biblical names, Pharez is mentioned in the Old Testament as the name of one of the twin sons of Judah and Tamar. This biblical connection adds an historical and religious dimension to the name. In the realm of genealogy research, Pharez can be a valuable find for those tracing their family roots. Pharez can be found on various platforms such as Facebook, LinkedIn, and Ancestry.com, where individuals may use it as a unique identifier for personal profiles or family trees.
